title: Scale-sensitivity of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for LLM-driven network-configuration repair (repaired preregistration)
research_question: Does a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline materially reduce incorrect or unsafe configuration repairs compared to raw LLM outputs as topology size and vendor heterogeneity increase?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: GVR yields a higher proportion of validator-passed (syntactically and semantically correct, regressions-free) repairs than raw LLM outputs (directional).
H2: The absolute benefit (GVR minus raw) decreases as topology size and cross-vendor heterogeneity increase (interaction effect).
exploratory_questions: Which failure modes (syntax, reachability regression, policy regression) dominate at each topology-size bin?
How many repair iterations (up to the preregistered cap) are required on average per topology bin before the verifier accepts a patch?
benchmark_scope: Cornetto-style repair scenarios (synthesized config faults) used as seed tasks
Synthetic topologies generated by the preregistered topology generator (see sampling_plan) with vendor heterogeneity parameters
model_scope: Primary hosted LLM: openai/gpt-4o (model_id: gpt-4o), temperature=0.0, max_tokens frozen
Secondary hosted LLM (fallback/robustness checks): openai/gpt-4o-mini (model_id: gpt-4o-mini), temperature=0.0
transformation_scope: Deterministic syntax parser and canonicalizer (per-vendor config grammars)
Deterministic reachability simulator (node-to-node path-checking over synthesized topology)
GVR orchestration loop: generate -> deterministic-verify -> if fail, produce repair request with structured fault-localization and up to M attempts
primary_estimand: Per-task difference in proportion-correct (validator-passed without regressions) between the final GVR output and the raw single-shot LLM output, aggregated per topology-size bin and pooled.
secondary_estimands: Average number of GVR iterations until verifier acceptance (per bin)
Per-failure-mode rates (syntax error, reachability regression, policy regression) for raw vs GVR
sampling_plan: Paired task design. Tasks are network-configuration repair instances produced by (a) selecting Cornetto-style seed fault scenarios and (b) synthesizing topologies with the preregistered generator (see topology spec). Topology-size bins: SMALL (<=10 nodes), MEDIUM (11–50 nodes), LARGE (51–200 nodes). Vendor-heterogeneity parameter h in [1..3] equals number of distinct device vendor grammars per topology. Randomization: tasks are assigned unique deterministic task IDs and RNG seeds (PRNG seed space reserved; seeds published). For each task (confirmed by seed): call 1 = raw LLM single-shot repair (fresh conversation, no history); call 2..call(1+M) = GVR generation attempts (fresh conversation per attempt). Inclusion: tasks where the model API returns a valid HTTP response and verifier completes are included; provider or infrastructure error tasks are logged, counted, and treated per missingness_plan. Preregistered seeds and the full topology generator code + 10 example seeds will be published alongside artifacts.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired comparison (McNemar test for paired binary outcomes) of per-task correctness (raw vs GVR) within each bin and pooled with logistic regression including method (GVR/raw), topology-size bin, heterogeneity parameter, and their interaction. Report absolute differences with 95% CIs via paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples using preregistered seeds) and exact two-sided McNemar p-values where cell counts permit. Secondary analyses: negative-binomial or Poisson regression of iteration counts; failure-mode contingency tables with chi-squared or Fisher exact tests as appropriate. All tests two-sided unless otherwise noted. Full code, seeds, raw outputs, verifier traces, and hashes will be published for reproducibility.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory tests: per-bin McNemar tests (3 bins). Control family-wise error for the three primary bin-level tests with Holm–Bonferroni. Pooled analysis reported without multiplicity correction (primary prespecified pooled estimand). Secondary/exploratory tests are reported as exploratory and not corrected unless explicitly stated.
missingness_plan: Technical/infrastructure failures (API errors, timeouts, verifier crashes): log and exclude from primary confirmatory analysis; report counts and describe in sensitivity analyses where excluded tasks are treated as failures for either method. If >10% of tasks are technical-failure-missing, run an additional preregistered recovery batch (same seeds) up to the retry policy; if still >10% missing, mark as protocol deviation and report results with conservative missingness sensitivity.

risk_factors: Cross-task leakage in model context if conversation not reset
Prompt-injection via task content causing verifier-escape
Dataset overlap between model pretraining and seed scenarios (unverifiable)
detection_procedures: Reset conversation context for every model call; verify via API call metadata.
Deterministic check of outputs for embedded prompt-like instruction tokens; flagged by parser.
Unique task IDs and hash checks on inputs/outputs to detect accidental duplication.
item_flagging_rules: Flag any model output containing >1 occurrence of the string patterns matching system-level instructions (e.g., 'ignore previous', 'do not follow')
Flag outputs that include device credentials or unexpected external URIs
Flag outputs that change configuration lines outside the fault-localization scope
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Flagged items are automatically excluded from primary confirmatory analysis and reported in a contamination report. Sensitivity analyses will re-include flagged items as failures to test robustness.
residual_uncertainty: Unknown overlap between model pretraining corpora and synthesized seeds (noncritical external-validity limitation)
Verifier-escape via subtle prompt-injection not captured by static string rules

budget_scenarios.description: Pilot and low-cost confirmatory run (reduced per-bin N).
transformations: Deterministic verifier (parser + reachability + policy oracle), GVR loop with M=3 attempts
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-bin N=120 tasks (SMALL/MEDIUM/LARGE). Worst-case model calls per task = 1 (raw) + M (3) = 4; 380 tasks including 20 pilot → 380*4 = 1520 calls. Fits well below the platform 10k call cap and enables quick runtime.

budget_scenarios.description: Balanced, preregistered primary study with conservative power assumptions.
transformations: Deterministic verifier (parser + reachability + policy oracle), GVR loop with M=3 attempts
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-bin N=180 tasks (SMALL/MEDIUM/LARGE). Worst-case model calls: 570 tasks (including 30 pilot) * 4 calls/task = 2280 model calls. Within the hosted API budget ceiling (10k) and estimated runtime boundary. Recommended for primary preregistered run to achieve >80% power under conservative assumptions (see power_plan).

budget_scenarios.description: High-power, more robust interaction test with larger per-bin N.
transformations: Deterministic verifier (parser + reachability + policy oracle), GVR loop with M=3 attempts
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-bin N=300 tasks; 950 tasks total including 50 pilot * 4 calls = 3800 calls. Still within the 10k limit but increases wall-clock and cost; useful only if additional budget is available.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Absolute difference in proportion-correct (GVR - raw) per topology-size bin and pooled.
power_plan.target_effect: Absolute improvement of 0.15 (15 percentage points) in proportion-correct for GVR vs raw (conservative, literature-informed).
power_plan.clustering_unit: Individual repair task (paired: raw and GVR outputs for the same task).
power_plan.calculation_method: Conservative sample-size reference computed via unpaired two-proportion z-test as an upper bound then acknowledging paired design efficiency. Using p_raw=0.60, p_gvr=0.75, alpha=0.05, power=0.8 yields ~153 per group (conservative). With paired design efficiency we set per-bin N=180 (recommended) to account for heterogeneity and to preserve power for interaction tests; per-bin N=180 => total confirmatory tasks = 540. Paired McNemar and logistic-regression-based power simulations (conducted offline with preregistered seeds) show >80% power to detect a 15ppt absolute improvement in pooled and per-bin analyses under conservative discordant-rate assumptions.
assumptions: GVR improves absolute correctness by ~0.15 in small/medium cases (F3/F2 evidence), smaller in large bins
Discordant-pair rates allow paired tests to have higher power than unpaired approximations
Max model calls per task = 4 (1 raw + up to M=3 GVR attempts)
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With per-bin N=180 and paired design, detectable absolute difference ≈0.10–0.12 with power ~0.8 depending on discordant-pair structure; we prespecify 0.15 for primary claim and report sensitivity curves for smaller effects.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute power under p_raw in {0.5,0.6,0.7} and effect sizes in {0.10,0.15,0.20}.
Assess power loss if up to 10% of tasks become technical-missing after retries.
Report results of logistic-regression interaction term across heterogeneous-simulated topologies.

transformation_families: Syntax parsers / canonicalizers per vendor (Cisco IOS, Juniper Junos, Arista EOS) implemented as deterministic grammars and unit-tested examples
Reachability simulator: deterministic graph-based path-checker using synthesized topology adjacency and route tables
Policy/regression oracle: deterministic ACL/policy checkers comparing pre-fault and post-patch behavior on canonical test flows
GVR orchestration deterministic state-machine (generate -> verify -> structured repair request -> generate)
semantic_equivalence_checks: For each accepted patch, run canonical test flows: expected connectivity set must be preserved or restored according to the seed fault specification.
Line-level canonicalization: whitespace/ordering-insensitive diff after canonicalization; semantic equivalence requires behavior-preserving changes only within the fault-localization scope.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject patch if syntax parser fails for any device vendor grammar.
Reject patch if reachability tests introduce any new end-to-end path failure for pre-specified canonical flows (regression).
Reject patch if patch modifies configuration lines outside the fault-localization scope more than a prespecified threshold (e.g., >3 unrelated lines).
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated deep-simulation audit on deterministic 5% sample of accepted patches per bin: run extended reachability and policy simulations (longer test-flows) and confirm acceptance. Audit selection is deterministic (hash-based) and reproducible.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Unit-test suite for the parser/canonicalizer with at least 50 vendor-specific examples per supported vendor; test-suite included in artifacts and executed prior to experiment to assert deterministic behavior.
residual_risks: Deterministic verifier may not capture dynamic operational constraints (timing, device-specific hidden semantics).
Vendor grammar coverage limited to declared vendors; other vendors treated as out-of-scope (noncritical external-validity).

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Verifier coverage: deterministic checks approximate operational correctness but may miss some device-specific semantics (construct-validity limitation; does not block the paired test).
Topology synthesis: synthetic topologies approximate production heterogeneity but may not fully represent private production networks (external-validity limitation).
Model pretraining overlap: unknown overlap between model pretraining corpora and synthetic seeds could bias results (noncritical for within-design comparison but affects generalization).
Prompt/template sensitivity: single-model design (gpt-4o) may not generalize to all LLMs; robustness checks with the secondary model are exploratory.
